subject.title: Cron sessions deliver hallucinated output instead of failing cleanly when tool calls fail

question: What should OpenClaw do by default for cron or unattended final assistant text when the same run recorded failed tools, missing required data, or no proof of the claimed side effect?
rationale: The remaining fix changes a security-sensitive delivery boundary and may alter existing cron behavior, so automation should not choose fail-open versus fail-closed semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed by default
options.body: Require structured successful recovery or explicit failure acknowledgement before cron/unattended delivery can publish final assistant text after tool failures.

options.title: Keep current default and add strict mode
options.body: Preserve current recoverable-warning behavior for existing cron jobs while adding an opt-in strict policy for users who need fail-closed unattended runs.

options.title: Plugin-only claim verification
options.body: Keep core cron finalization unchanged and leave broader success-claim verification to ClawHub/plugin implementations.

recommendation.title: Fail closed by default
recommendation.body: Require structured successful recovery or explicit failure acknowledgement before cron/unattended delivery can publish final assistant text after tool failures.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current source-history signal on the relevant cron and agent-runtime files and the decision is a default runtime policy choice.
